description: This file defines various classes related to HTTP security authentication schemes in FastAPI, including Basic, Bearer, Digest, and general HTTP authentication base class. It includes data models representing credentials and helper methods for authentication handling.

classes.name: HTTPBasicCredentials
classes.description: Data model for storing HTTP Basic authentication credentials containing username and password.

classes.name: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
classes.description: Data model for storing HTTP authorization credentials with scheme and credentials.

classes.name: HTTPBase
classes.description: Base class for HTTP authentication schemes, providing common functionality for scheme handling and error management.

classes.name: HTTPBasic
classes.description: Implementation of HTTP Basic authentication scheme, including optional realm and error handling.

classes.name: HTTPBearer
classes.description: Implementation of HTTP Bearer token authentication with options for scheme name and error handling.

classes.name: HTTPDigest
classes.description: Stub class for HTTP Digest authentication, intended for integration with OpenAPI, not a complete implementation.

methods.name: dict[str,str] make_authenticate_headers(self)
methods.description: Constructs headers for challenge responses based on the scheme.

methods.name: HTTPException make_not_authenticated_error(self)
methods.description: Creates an HTTP 401 Unauthorized error with appropriate headers.

methods.name: Optional[HTTPBasicCredentials] __call__( self, request: Request )
methods.description: Handles the request to extract and validate the authorization credentials from headers for different schemes.

                " ), ] = None, auto_error: Annotated[ bool, Doc( "
                By default, if the HTTP Bearer token is not provided (in an
                `Authorization` header), `HTTPBearer` will automatically cancel the
                request and send the client an error.

                If `auto_error` is set to `False`, when the HTTP Bearer token
                is not available, instead of erroring out, the dependency result will
                be `None`.

                This is useful when you want to have optional authentication.

                It is also useful when you want to have authentication that can be
                provided in one of multiple optional ways (for example, in an HTTP
                Bearer token or in a cookie).
